rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human nature is marked by deficiency, injustice, and ignorance, so people are liable to distraction by accumulation unless God grants faith.
rows.anchor: فالقصور شأنه , والظلم طبعه , والجهل جبلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general judgment on humankind applies to all by nature, while the very few God preserves from human defects are excepted.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الحكم على الجنس حكما على الكل لأنهم ليس لهم من ذواتهم إلا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those excepted are few relative to the people in loss; God preserves them from the inclinations and shortcomings of human nature.
rows.anchor: استثناهم سبحانه وتعالى لأنهم قليل جدا بالنسبة غلى أهل الخسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith means affirming what is necessarily known to have been brought by the Prophet: God's oneness, angels, books, messengers, and the Last Day.
rows.anchor: أي أوجدوا الإيمان وهو التصديق بما علم بالضرورة مجيء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم به من توحيده سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense wording encourages entry into the religion even at its lowest initial degree and promises salvation to whoever fulfills its conditions.
rows.anchor: ولعل حكمة التعبير بالماضي الحث على الدخول في الدين ولو على أدنى الدرجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are rational animals whose perfection lies in voluntary practical action, rather than being driven by overpowering animal appetite.
rows.anchor: وكان كمال حيوانيته في القوة العملية للحركة بالإرادة لا بمقتضى الشهوة القاسرة البهيمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous deeds mean following commands and avoiding prohibitions in worship and ordinary dealings, such as prayer and buying and selling.
rows.anchor: وهو اتبع الأوامر واجتناب النواهي في العبادات كالصلاة والعادات كالبيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through righteous deeds, believers become Muslims after being believers, trade the world for the next life, and escape distraction by accumulation.
rows.anchor: فكانوا بهذا مسلمين بعد أن كانوا مؤمنين فاشتروا الآخرة بالدنيا فلم يلههم التكاثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person cannot escape loss merely by perfecting himself; he must also complete others, since prophets were sent to guide and religion requires communal mutual exhortation.
rows.anchor: لا ينتفي عنه مطلق الخسر - إلا بتكميل غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth includes everything the sacred law deems correct, whether speech, deed, belief, action, or abstention.
rows.anchor: وهو كل ما حكم الشرع بصحته فلا يصح بوجه نفيه من قول أو عمل أو اعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual counsel is necessary because religion is sustained through enjoining right and forbidding wrong, which arise from an illuminated heart and require community.
rows.anchor: وكان الدين لا يقوم , وإذا قام لا يتم إلا بالأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر الناشئ عن نور القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous become beneficent by advising one another in truth and perfecting others through practical virtue.
rows.anchor: فكانوا محسنين , والتكميل في القوة العملية باجتلاب الخيور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counsel in patience is needed because the righteous face hostility from the unjust majority and must endure obedience, vindicating truth, resisting wrong, and the resulting harm until death.
rows.anchor: وهم الأغلب في كل زمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual exhortation and patience complete practical perfection while preserving the earlier intellectual perfection; worship aims at Paradise externally and an inward light drawing one near to God.
rows.anchor: وهي هنا أمران : خارج عن العامل وهو الجنة , وداخل قائم به وهو النور المقرب من الحق سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording 'mutually enjoined' signals gentleness in commanding right and forbidding wrong, using soft counsel to the utmost effort.
rows.anchor: واختير التعبير بالوصية إشارة إلى الرفق في الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is the human essence and distillation, attained by disciplining the self into obedience and adherence to the Sunna and community until it becomes habitual.
rows.anchor: والصبر هو خلاصة الإنسان وسره وصفاوته وزبدته وعصارته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the fourteen words as alluding to permission for jihad in the fourteenth prophetic year, the Hijra year, when jihad embodied enjoining right and the truth prevailed at Badr.
rows.anchor: وهي أربع عشرة كلمة تشير إلى أن في اسنة الرابعة عشر من النبوة يكون الإذن في الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Confederates, the believers were terrified, as eyes turned and hearts reached their throats.
rows.anchor: وفي الأحزاب زاغت الأبصار وبلغت القلوب الحناجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites 3:173, where those who warned that enemies had assembled against the believers only increased their faith, and they answered that God was sufficient for them.
rows.anchor: الذي قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم فاخشوهم فزادهم إيمانا وقالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet said after the Confederates that thereafter the Muslims would campaign against their foes rather than be raided by them.
rows.anchor: أسفرت عاقبة الصبر فيها عما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عند ذهابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding four pronouns to the word count alludes to year nine, the difficult Tabuk expedition, whose patient hardship was followed by arriving delegations and honor for Islam.
rows.anchor: فإذا ضممت إليها الضمائر الأربعة أشارت إلى سنة تسع , وقد كانت فيها غزوة تبوك وهي غزوة العسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of al-Humazah is to expose the greatest losing faction, whom accumulation distracts; the surah's name signals this meaning.
rows.anchor: مقصودها بيان الحزب الأكبر الخاسر الذي أهاه التكاثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as possessing complete might and just judgment, extending outward mercy to both misers and givers, and completing His favor for chosen servants.
rows.anchor: الذي له تمام العز وهو الحكم العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is also called al-Din, Ara'ayta, and al-Takdhib; its purpose is to show denial of resurrection and recompense as the root of vile character and contempt for people's rights.
rows.anchor: وتسمى الدين وتسمى أرأيت والتكذيب . مقصودها التنبيه على أن التكذيب بالبعث لأجل الجزاء أبو الخبائث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its names clearly point to its theme on reflection: it directly forbids vice and indirectly calls people toward noble conduct.
rows.anchor: داعية إلى المعالي بإفهامها وتلويحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala praises God's perfection, mercy to both good and bad, and the completion of grace for His close servants through the joy of communion.
rows.anchor: الذي تعالت عظمته عن كل شائبة نقص فكان له كل كمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding dealings with Quraysh show that God punishes transgression and treats people with wise gentleness, so He will not leave them without recompense; Quraysh were commanded to thank Him through exclusive worship.
rows.anchor: فكان معرفا بأن فاعله لا يترك الناس سدى من غير جزاء , وأمرهم آخر قريش بشكر نعمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in recompense motivates noble character and restrains vice; the author marvels that anyone could deny it despite the clear evidence of divine wisdom, and says the surah depicts the denier repulsively to urge belief.
rows.anchor: وعجب ممن يكذب بالجزاء مع وضوح الدلالة عليه بحمة الحكيم , ووصف المكذب به بأوصاف هم منها في غاية النفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct address 'Have you seen?' is aimed at the Prophet as the community's leader, since he alone fully understands this matter.
rows.anchor: فقال خاصا بالخطاب رأس الأمة إشارة إلى أنه لا يفهم هذا الأمر حق فهمه غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here 'Have you seen?' means 'tell me'; since it governs two objects, the omitted second object is understood as asking whether the denier deserves punishment.
rows.anchor: ولما كان فعل الرؤية بمعنى أخبرني , المتعدي إلى مفعولين , كان تقدير المفعول الثاني : أليس جديرا بالانتقام منه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: He links this surah to earlier warnings about human ignorance and injustice and cites the ungrateful person, humanity in loss, and the man who thinks wealth makes him immortal.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما تضمنت السور المتقدمة من الوعيد لمن انطوى على ما ذكر فيها

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: He says those earlier traits also produce obsession with accumulation, slander and mockery, and pride in the people of the Elephant.
rows.anchor: وانجر أثناء ذلك مما تثيره هذه الصفات الأولية ما ذكر فيها أيضا كالشغل بالتكاثر , والطعن على الناس ولمزهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: He notes that people affiliated with Islam may push an orphan from his rights or fail to care for him, discourage feeding the poor, neglect prayer, show off, and withhold zakat or necessities.
rows.anchor: كدع اليتيم , وهو دفعه عن حقه وعدم الرفق به , وعدم الحض على طعام المسكين , والتغافل عن الصلاة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: He reads these traits as those of a denier who expects no judgment, while observing that such acts can occur among Muslims without every person who commits them necessarily being a denier.
rows.anchor: فأخبر سبحانه وتعالى أنه من صفات من يكذب بيوم الدين ولا ينتظر الجزاء والحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares this trait-based description to hadiths that call one with four specified traits a pure hypocrite and say a fornicator is not a believer while committing the act.
rows.anchor: فمن هذا القبيل عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These people may do lesser good ostentatiously but are so dominated by greed that they cannot even show off by giving a trivial benefit; the best people in God's sight benefit His dependents most.
rows.anchor: إشعارا بأن أحب الخلق إلى الله أنفعهم لعياله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb 'withhold' suggests repeated behavior, and omission of its first object generalizes the withholding to everyone, even the highly esteemed.
rows.anchor: وحذف المفعول الأول تعمما حتى يشمل كل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ma'un includes financial rights and small useful items, such as ordinary household objects people lend one another.
rows.anchor: حقوق الأموال والشيء اليسير من المنافع مثل إعارة التافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat of woe applies to withholding what must be given, including surplus pasture or water and zakat, as well as similar obligatory rights owed to the needy.
rows.anchor: ينبغي حمل ذلك على منع ما يجب بذله مثل فضل الكلأ والماء والزكاة ونحوه ليكون موجبا للويل

rows.speaker: علي وابن عمر والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: They interpret al-ma'un as zakat.
rows.anchor: وعلى الزكاة حمله علي وابن عمر رضي الله عنهما والحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some explain al-ma'un as a small thing, such as water or a loaned household item, or as zakat, which is small in relation to the wealth from which it is due.
rows.anchor: هو في اللغة الشيء اليسير , ولذلك فسره بعضهم بالماء وبعضهم بما يعار

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation takes al-ma'un to mean every gift or benefit.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو كل عطية أو منفعة

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub derives ma'un as a fa'ul form from ma'n, meaning recognized kindness.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب : هو فاعول من المعن , والمعن : المعروف

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says al-ma'un meant gifts and benefits in pre-Islamic times and zakat in Islam.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : الماعون في الجاهلية العطاء والمنفعة وفي الإسلام الزكاة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to interpret al-ma'un as a loan or lending; al-Harawi records this through Abd al-Haqq al-Ishbili's book.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنما

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says the root meaning of al-ma'un is the benefit of any thing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جرير : وأصل الماعون من كل شيء منفعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Withholding al-ma'un shows extreme denial: these people disdain a major religious pillar while magnifying tiny worldly matters; the cause is denial of recompense.
rows.anchor: فدل ذلك على أنهم بلغوا نهاية التكذيب باستهانتهم بأعظم دعائم الدين واستعظامهم لأدنى أمور الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending returns to the beginning because denial of judgment breeds neglect of people and obedience to God, contempt for the weak, and ostentation; the surah urges the opposite, noble character.
rows.anchor: وهذا الآخر كما ترى هو الأول لأن الذي جر إليه هو التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who withhold even trifles deserve to be denied al-Kawthar at the gathering, and the surah's final point echoes its opening.
rows.anchor: ومن منع هذه الأشياء التافهه كان جديرا بأن يمنع ورود الكوثر في يوم المحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven-verse al-Ma'un parallels seven-verse al-Anfal in number and in turning its ending back to its opening; al-Anfal expands the same lesson, so readers should notice the connection.
rows.anchor: وكما التقى آخرها بأولها التقت السورة كلها مع مناظرتها في العدد من أول القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anfal 8:4 describes true believers as those who establish prayer and spend from God's provision, connecting with al-Ma'un's themes of prayer and giving.
rows.anchor: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah has twenty-five words; counting from the beginning of prophethood points to year twelve AH, when Abu Bakr had eliminated the apostates and zakat-refusers, exposing their earlier prayer and almsgiving as mere show.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن عدة كلماته خمس وعشرون كلمة فإذا اعتبرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr's campaigns ended in that year with the defeat of Banu Hanifa at Yamama, people of al-Nujayr in Kindah, and al-Aswad al-Ansi in Sanaa.
rows.anchor: ولم تمض تلك السنة إلا وقد فرغ منهم بالفراغ من بني حنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The twenty-five words plus the four-word basmala point to year sixteen AH: Arab polytheists, Christians, and Magians had left the peninsula, most converting and the rest going to Byzantine lands.
rows.anchor: وما مضت سنة ست عشرة الموازية لعدد الكلمات بالبسملة - وذلك في أوائل خلافة الفاروق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woe fell on showy worshippers who had been invited by their Prophet to pray but turned away, while other people followed them.
rows.anchor: فحل الويل بالمرائين من أهل الصلاة فإنهم الذين أتى إليهم نبيهم صلى الله عليه وسلم بالصلاة فأعرضوا عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counting pronouns is unsuitable because the religion had become openly manifest and unobstructed; counting letters is also unnecessary after its public triumph became clear.
rows.anchor: ولم يصح في هذه السورة اعتبار الضمائر لأن الدين في هذا الحد كان قد ظهر على كل ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kawthar is also called al-Nahr; its purpose is to announce a gift of every possible good, and both names clearly convey that bounty, since camel sacrifice represents supreme generosity among Arabs.
rows.anchor: مقصودها المنحة بكل خير يمكن أن يكون ، واسمها الكوثر واضح في ذلك وكذا النحر لأنه معروف في نحر الإبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as the supreme, most generous king, whose generosity reaches all creatures in varying measure and whose guidance and covenant are specially granted to His community.
rows.anchor: الملك الأعظم الجواد الأكرم الذي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Surat al-Layl was revealed in Mecca.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن الضريس والنحاس وابن مردويه والبيهقي عن ابن عباس قال : نزلت سورة

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr also reports that the surah was revealed in Mecca.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن الزبير مثله

rows.speaker: جابر بن سمرة
rows.claim: Jabir ibn Samura reports that the Prophet recited this surah and similar ones during the noon and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي في سننه عن جابر بن سمرة قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ في الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A weak-chain report from Ibn Abbas says the surah was revealed after a poor father complained that a palm owner entered his home and snatched dates from his children; the Prophet offered the owner a palm in Paradise, but he declined.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم بسند ضعيف عن ابن عباس : «أن رجلاً كانت له نخلة فرعها في دار رجل فقير ذي عيال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the same weak report, another man bought the palm for forty palms and gave it to the Prophet, who gave it to the poor family; the surah was then revealed.
rows.anchor: فأتى رسول الله : فقال أعطني ما أعطيت الرجل إن أنا أخذتها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the surah concerns generosity and miserliness.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس قال : إني لأقول هذه السورة نزلت في السماحة والبخل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the night as becoming dark.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن عباس { والليل إذا يغشى } قال : إذا أظلم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains the phrase as night approaching and covering everything.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن جبير { والليل إذا يغشى } قال : إذا أقبل فغطى كل شيء

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: Alqama reports Abdullah's reading as 'by the male and female'; Abu al-Darda confirms that he heard the Prophet recite it that way and rejects the reading 'Who created the male and female.'
rows.anchor: قال : علقمة : «والذكر والأنثى » فقال أبو الدرداء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas retained eighteen readings from Abdullah ibn Masud alongside Zayd ibn Thabit's reading, including 'by the male and female'; he says it is an oath that should not be broken off.
rows.anchor: وفي الليل : «والذكر والأنثى » قال : هو قسم فلا تقطعوه

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq reports Abdullah's connected reading: 'By the night when it covers, by the day when it appears, and by the male and female.'
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق قال ؛ في قراءة عبد الله : «والليل إذا يغشى والنهار إذا تجلى والذكر والأنثى »

none: Verse text only; the segment gives no commentary or reports.
